scene.label: Act 1, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. Troy. Before Priam's palace.

lines.text: Call here my varlet; I'll unarm again.
lines.plainText: Call here my varlet I'll unarm again

lines.text: Why should I war without the walls of Troy
lines.plainText: Why should I war without the walls of Troy

lines.text: That find such cruel battle here within?
lines.plainText: That find such cruel battle here within

lines.text: Each Trojan that is master of his heart,
lines.plainText: Each Trojan that is master of his heart

lines.text: Let him to field; Troilus, alas! hath none.
lines.plainText: Let him to field Troilus alas hath none

lines.text: Will this gear ne'er be mended?
lines.plainText: Will this gear ne'er be mended

lines.text: The Greeks are strong, and skilful to their strength,
lines.plainText: The Greeks are strong and skilful to their strength

lines.text: Fierce to their skill, and to their fierceness valiant;
lines.plainText: Fierce to their skill and to their fierceness valiant

lines.text: But I am weaker than a woman's tear,
lines.plainText: But I am weaker than a woman's tear

lines.text: Tamer than sleep, fonder than ignorance,
lines.plainText: Tamer than sleep fonder than ignorance

lines.text: Less valiant than the virgin in the night,
lines.plainText: Less valiant than the virgin in the night

lines.text: And skilless as unpractis'd infancy.
lines.plainText: And skilless as unpractis'd infancy

lines.text: Well, I have told you enough of this; for my part, I'll not meddle nor make no farther. He that will have a cake out of the wheat must tarry the grinding.
lines.plainText: Well I have told you enough of this for my part I'll not meddle nor make no farther He that will have a cake out of the wheat must tarry the grinding

lines.text: Have I not tarried?
lines.plainText: Have I not tarried

lines.text: Ay, the grinding; but you must tarry the bolting.
lines.plainText: Ay the grinding but you must tarry the bolting

lines.text: Have I not tarried?
lines.plainText: Have I not tarried

lines.text: Ay, the bolting; but you must tarry the leavening.
lines.plainText: Ay the bolting but you must tarry the leavening

lines.text: Still have I tarried.
lines.plainText: Still have I tarried

lines.text: Ay, to the leavening; but here's yet in the word 'hereafter' the kneading, the making of the cake, the heating of the oven, and the baking; nay, you must stay the cooling too, or you may chance burn your lips.
lines.plainText: Ay to the leavening but here's yet in the word 'hereafter' the kneading the making of the cake the heating of the oven and the baking nay you must stay the cooling too or you may chance burn your lips

lines.text: Patience herself, what goddess e'er she be,
lines.plainText: Patience herself what goddess e'er she be

lines.text: Doth lesser blench at suff'rance than I do.
lines.plainText: Doth lesser blench at suff'rance than I do

lines.text: At Priam's royal table do I sit;
lines.plainText: At Priam's royal table do I sit

lines.text: And when fair Cressid comes into my thoughts,
lines.plainText: And when fair Cressid comes into my thoughts

lines.text: So, traitor! 'when she comes'! when she is thence?
lines.plainText: So traitor 'when she comes' when she is thence

lines.text: Well, she look'd yesternight fairer than ever I saw her look, or any woman else.
lines.plainText: Well she look'd yesternight fairer than ever I saw her look or any woman else

lines.text: I was about to tell thee: when my heart,
lines.plainText: I was about to tell thee when my heart

lines.text: As wedged with a sigh, would rive in twain,
lines.plainText: As wedged with a sigh would rive in twain

lines.text: Lest Hector or my father should perceive me,
lines.plainText: Lest Hector or my father should perceive me

lines.text: I have, as when the sun doth light a storm,
lines.plainText: I have as when the sun doth light a storm

lines.text: Buried this sigh in wrinkle of a smile.
lines.plainText: Buried this sigh in wrinkle of a smile

lines.text: But sorrow that is couch'd in seeming gladness
lines.plainText: But sorrow that is couch'd in seeming gladness

lines.text: Is like that mirth fate turns to sudden sadness.
lines.plainText: Is like that mirth fate turns to sudden sadness

lines.text: An her hair were not somewhat darker than Helen's, well, go to, there were no more comparison between the women. But, for my part, she is my kinswoman; I would not, as they term it, praise her, but I would somebody had heard her talk yesterday, as I did. I will not dispraise your sister Cassandra's wit; but—
lines.plainText: An her hair were not somewhat darker than Helen's well go to there were no more comparison between the women But for my part she is my kinswoman I would not as they term it praise her but I would somebody had heard her talk yesterday as I did I will not dispraise your sister Cassandra's wit but

lines.text: O Pandarus! I tell thee, Pandarus,
lines.plainText: O Pandarus I tell thee Pandarus

lines.text: When I do tell thee there my hopes lie drown'd,
lines.plainText: When I do tell thee there my hopes lie drown'd

lines.text: Reply not in how many fathoms deep
lines.plainText: Reply not in how many fathoms deep

lines.text: They lie indrench'd. I tell thee I am mad
lines.plainText: They lie indrench'd I tell thee I am mad

lines.text: In Cressid's love. Thou answer'st 'She is fair';
lines.plainText: In Cressid's love Thou answer'st 'She is fair'

lines.text: Pour'st in the open ulcer of my heart
lines.plainText: Pour'st in the open ulcer of my heart

lines.text: Her eyes, her hair, her cheek, her gait, her voice,
lines.plainText: Her eyes her hair her cheek her gait her voice

lines.text: Handlest in thy discourse. O! that her hand,
lines.plainText: Handlest in thy discourse O that her hand

lines.text: In whose comparison all whites are ink
lines.plainText: In whose comparison all whites are ink

lines.text: Writing their own reproach; to whose soft seizure
lines.plainText: Writing their own reproach to whose soft seizure

lines.text: The cygnet's down is harsh, and spirit of sense
lines.plainText: The cygnet's down is harsh and spirit of sense

lines.text: Hard as the palm of ploughman! This thou tell'st me,
lines.plainText: Hard as the palm of ploughman This thou tell'st me

lines.text: As true thou tell'st me, when I say I love her;
lines.plainText: As true thou tell'st me when I say I love her

lines.text: But, saying thus, instead of oil and balm,
lines.plainText: But saying thus instead of oil and balm

lines.text: Thou lay'st in every gash that love hath given me
lines.plainText: Thou lay'st in every gash that love hath given me

lines.text: The knife that made it.
lines.plainText: The knife that made it

lines.text: I speak no more than truth.
lines.plainText: I speak no more than truth

lines.text: Thou dost not speak so much.
lines.plainText: Thou dost not speak so much

lines.text: Faith, I'll not meddle in't. Let her be as she is: if she be fair, 'tis the better for her; and she be not, she has the mends in her own hands.
lines.plainText: Faith I'll not meddle in't Let her be as she is if she be fair 'tis the better for her and she be not she has the mends in her own hands

lines.text: Good Pandarus! How now, Pandarus!
lines.plainText: Good Pandarus How now Pandarus

lines.text: I have had my labour for my travail, ill thought on of her and ill thought on of you; gone between and between, but small thanks for my labour.
lines.plainText: I have had my labour for my travail ill thought on of her and ill thought on of you gone between and between but small thanks for my labour

lines.text: What! art thou angry, Pandarus? What! with me?
lines.plainText: What art thou angry Pandarus What with me

lines.text: Because she's kin to me, therefore she's not so fair as Helen. And she were not kin to me, she would be as fair on Friday as Helen is on Sunday. But what care I? I care not and she were a blackamoor; 'tis all one to me.
lines.plainText: Because she's kin to me therefore she's not so fair as Helen And she were not kin to me she would be as fair on Friday as Helen is on Sunday But what care I I care not and she were a blackamoor 'tis all one to me

lines.text: Say I she is not fair?
lines.plainText: Say I she is not fair

lines.text: I do not care whether you do or no. She's a fool to stay behind her father. Let her to the Greeks; and so I'll tell her the next time I see her. For my part, I'll meddle nor make no more i' the matter.
lines.plainText: I do not care whether you do or no She's a fool to stay behind her father Let her to the Greeks and so I'll tell her the next time I see her For my part I'll meddle nor make no more i' the matter

lines.text: Pandarus—
lines.plainText: Pandarus

lines.text: Not I.
lines.plainText: Not I

lines.text: Sweet Pandarus—
lines.plainText: Sweet Pandarus

lines.text: Pray you, speak no more to me: I will leave all as I found it, and there an end.
lines.plainText: Pray you speak no more to me I will leave all as I found it and there an end

lines.text: Peace, you ungracious clamours! Peace, rude sounds!
lines.plainText: Peace you ungracious clamours Peace rude sounds

lines.text: Fools on both sides! Helen must needs be fair,
lines.plainText: Fools on both sides Helen must needs be fair

lines.text: When with your blood you daily paint her thus.
lines.plainText: When with your blood you daily paint her thus

lines.text: I cannot fight upon this argument;
lines.plainText: I cannot fight upon this argument

lines.text: It is too starv'd a subject for my sword.
lines.plainText: It is too starv'd a subject for my sword

lines.text: But Pandarus, O gods! how do you plague me!
lines.plainText: But Pandarus O gods how do you plague me

lines.text: I cannot come to Cressid but by Pandar;
lines.plainText: I cannot come to Cressid but by Pandar

lines.text: And he's as tetchy to be woo'd to woo
lines.plainText: And he's as tetchy to be woo'd to woo

lines.text: As she is stubborn-chaste against all suit.
lines.plainText: As she is stubbornchaste against all suit

lines.text: Tell me, Apollo, for thy Daphne's love,
lines.plainText: Tell me Apollo for thy Daphne's love

lines.text: What Cressid is, what Pandar, and what we?
lines.plainText: What Cressid is what Pandar and what we

lines.text: Her bed is India; there she lies, a pearl;
lines.plainText: Her bed is India there she lies a pearl

lines.text: Between our Ilium and where she resides
lines.plainText: Between our Ilium and where she resides

lines.text: Let it be call'd the wild and wandering flood;
lines.plainText: Let it be call'd the wild and wandering flood

lines.text: Ourself the merchant, and this sailing Pandar
lines.plainText: Ourself the merchant and this sailing Pandar

lines.text: Our doubtful hope, our convoy, and our bark.
lines.plainText: Our doubtful hope our convoy and our bark

lines.text: How now, Prince Troilus! Wherefore not afield?
lines.plainText: How now Prince Troilus Wherefore not afield

lines.text: Because not there. This woman's answer sorts,
lines.plainText: Because not there This woman's answer sorts

lines.text: For womanish it is to be from thence.
lines.plainText: For womanish it is to be from thence

lines.text: What news, Aeneas, from the field today?
lines.plainText: What news Aeneas from the field today

lines.text: That Paris is returned home, and hurt.
lines.plainText: That Paris is returned home and hurt

lines.text: By whom, Aeneas?
lines.plainText: By whom Aeneas

lines.text: Troilus, by Menelaus.
lines.plainText: Troilus by Menelaus

lines.text: Let Paris bleed: 'tis but a scar to scorn;
lines.plainText: Let Paris bleed 'tis but a scar to scorn

lines.text: Paris is gor'd with Menelaus' horn.
lines.plainText: Paris is gor'd with Menelaus' horn

lines.text: Hark what good sport is out of town today!
lines.plainText: Hark what good sport is out of town today

lines.text: Better at home, if 'would I might' were 'may.'
lines.plainText: Better at home if 'would I might' were 'may'

lines.text: But to the sport abroad. Are you bound thither?
lines.plainText: But to the sport abroad Are you bound thither

lines.text: In all swift haste.
lines.plainText: In all swift haste

lines.text: Come, go we then together.
lines.plainText: Come go we then together
